common_name: Lemon Zest Mango (Dwarf Container Mango with Citrusy Flavor)

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun in well-drained soil, or grow in a large container to shelter from frost; Lemon Zest is a true dwarf mango bred for container culture, staying compact enough for a patio pot.

directions: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun in well-drained soil, or grow in a large container that can be moved under cover before frost. Lemon Zest is a true dwarf mango, bred specifically for container culture and small landscapes, staying compact enough to manage on a sunny patio while still bearing full-sized fruit. Its bright yellow, fiberless flesh carries a distinctive sweet-tart, citrusy note that gives the cultivar its name, setting it apart from the purely sweet flavor of most mango cultivars. Because it stays small, Lemon Zest is one of the more practical mango choices for zone 9 gardeners who want to grow mango in a container that can be sheltered through winter rather than risking an in-ground planting. Reduce irrigation as fruit nears ripeness to concentrate flavor, and protect the tree from any frost, since even brief freezing temperatures can damage or kill mango wood.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Mango Growing in the Home Landscape
Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden — Mango Cultivar Notes

common_name: Cotton Candy Mango (Dwarf Sweet Container Mango)

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun in well-drained soil, or grow in a large container to shelter from frost; Cotton Candy is a dwarf mango prized for exceptionally sweet, low-fiber flesh on a compact tree.

directions: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun in well-drained soil, or grow in a large container that can be moved under cover before frost. Cotton Candy is a dwarf mango bred for a small, manageable size and exceptionally sweet, nearly fiberless flesh with a soft, dessert-like flavor that has made it a popular choice among home growers seeking a compact tree without sacrificing fruit quality. Its small stature suits container growing in zone 9, where in-ground plantings risk winter damage, allowing the tree to be sheltered during freezes. Reduce irrigation as fruit nears ripeness to concentrate sugars and flavor, and protect the tree from any frost, since even brief freezing temperatures can damage or kill mango wood.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Mango Growing in the Home Landscape
Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden — Mango Cultivar Notes

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun in well-drained soil, or grow in a container to shelter from frost; Condo is one of the smallest mango cultivars available, bred specifically for balconies and small container gardens.

directions: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun in well-drained soil, or grow in a container that can be moved under cover before frost. Condo is one of the smallest mango cultivars in cultivation, bred specifically for balcony and patio container growing, staying under 6 feet even at maturity while still producing full-sized, flavorful fruit. Its extreme dwarf habit makes it the most practical mango option for gardeners with very limited space or those who need to bring the tree indoors or into a greenhouse for winter protection in zone 9 and cooler areas. Reduce irrigation as fruit nears ripeness to concentrate sugars and flavor, and protect the tree from any frost, since even brief freezing temperatures can damage or kill mango wood.
